questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8101: On its balance sheet, Foxglove Company lists accounts payable of $10,600, accrued liabilities of $3,900, and unearned revenue of $350. What are total current liabilities?

options.misconception: subtracts one liability from another
omits unearned revenue from the current liability total
reports only the smallest liability balance

questions.explanation: Every obligation due within a year belongs in current liabilities, so $10,600 plus $3,900 plus $350 totals $14,850. Omitting unearned revenue would understate obligations because that balance represents a duty to deliver goods or services.
questions.hint: Add every obligation that must be settled within one year.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8102: Foxglove Works issues a $10,250 bond paying 6 percent annual interest. What is the annual cash interest payment?

options.misconception: divides by the rate instead of multiplying by it
uses sixty percent instead of six percent of face value
treats the face value itself as the interest payment

questions.explanation: Cash interest on a bond equals face value times the stated rate, so $10,250 times six percent is $615 each year. Dividing by the rate or using the face value ignores how a coupon payment is calculated.
questions.hint: Multiply face value by the stated coupon rate.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8103: A $9,900 bond issued at a discount pays $2,850 of cash interest this period and has $550 of discount amortization. What is interest expense?

options.misconception: uses the coupon on face value rather than effective expense
subtracts discount amortization from cash interest
uses only cash interest and ignores the discount amortization

questions.explanation: When bonds are issued at a discount, interest expense exceeds the cash paid because the discount amortization is an additional financing cost, so $2,850 plus $550 gives $3,400. Subtracting the amortization would describe a premium bond instead.
questions.hint: A discount increases interest expense above the cash paid.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8104: Kestrel Traders has 51 shares of 6 percent preferred stock with a $8 par value. What is the annual preferred dividend?

questions.stem: Case 8107: On January 8, 2024, Oakmont Co. repurchases its own shares from investors for $8,500 in cash. What entry records the treasury stock purchase?
